approach: Add `check_defined_terms(reading, request)` to crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs as one `step!` in `refusing_check`, after `check_environment_reach` and before `check_boundary_and_repo_files`. It returns Ok for a reading with no capability, a question or no deliverable, as `check_outcome_state` does. Otherwise it reduces the request to plain prose, finds the whole words ladder, rung, tier and layer (plural and possessive too), and refuses when a used term has no `Term <word>:` assumption. Plain prose leaves out five things: (1) hestia's generated root-cause lines, skipped by exact shape; (2) NEW, finding 1: the text Athena's `approve_request` generates. When the request holds its opening sentence 'A person approved this proposal from the steward role.', the line 'Rung of the requirements ladder: ', the 'Proposal: ... (key ... queued at ...' line and everything from the '## Source' line on (the copied source and evidence) are cited content and are skipped. (3) Quoted spans. (4) Parenthesised example lists. (5) Code-like tokens containing `/`, `_` or `::`. The approval title (first line) and the hand-written parts stay checked. Tests build the accepted cases from the real generators: `hestia::root_cause_request` and `work_decisions::approve_request`, the latter against a temporary git repository made with `athena_git::Git` and `tempfile`, both already dependencies of athena-core. Shapes tests pin each generator's line shapes so a rewording fails visibly. The existing athena-cli tests that approve work (work_decisions.rs:96, drain.rs:5328, 6210, 6276) are the regression proof that real approvals still reach `Proposed`. The cited-jobs replay becomes g6vy by `check_outcome_state`, 7bf8 by `check_defined_terms`, 0wtc by none. The rule is also an eighth `READING_RULES` line in briefs.rs. A CHANGELOG entry and D164 declare 'expected 3% of newly refused readings' as an estimate over hand-written requests only. D164 lists the Athena generators checked and excluded and the false-refusal classes, and hands any narrowing of tier or layer to the user. Revision (findings 2 and 3): step 8 no longer has an at-or-under-8% branch. A held send-back lets the producer change only the prose pre-pass, never the four words.

decisions.choice: Match structural words in plain request prose only: a `plain_request_prose` pre-pass, then the existing `request_words` tokenizer (reading.rs:3507), then whole-word comparison (term, term+s, trailing `'s` stripped first).
decisions.reason: `request_words` splits all text and ignores quoting, and its tokens keep `'` between letters, so "ladder's" would match nothing. The 7bf8 request quotes 'a ladder of requirements' and also uses the term in plain prose, so the pre-pass must drop the first and keep the second. Whole-word tokens keep stepladder, delayer, `ladder.md` and `layer_count` out.

rejected.option: Run `request_words` over the whole request
rejected.why: It ignores quoting, so generated requests that only quote the words would be refused.

rejected.option: Substring match
rejected.why: It refuses stepladder and delayer, which criterion 3 requires to pass.

rejected.option: Treat every parenthesised span as a non-use
rejected.why: It hides real uses such as '(the ladder, which ranks requirements)'.

decisions.choice: Skip hestia's generated lines by exact shape. An `Introspection ` line is skipped only if it also holds ' (job ' and '); prevention it proposed:' (hestia.rs:486-488). `Failure class: `, `Cause: ` and `Fix the root cause of a repeated failure: ` lines are skipped only when the request also holds 'The same cause has produced failures in more than one job.' (hestia.rs:467).
decisions.reason: Those lines carry free prose from earlier introspections. Bare prefixes would drop a hand-written 'Introspection of the ladder is needed.' or 'Cause: the ladder has no rung'. The anchor sentence ties the skip to text Athena generated.

rejected.option: Skip any line that starts with introspection, cause: or failure class:
rejected.why: Case-insensitive bare prefixes drop hand-written lines that use a term.

rejected.option: Rely on quote stripping alone
rejected.why: The generated Cause and prevention text is free prose, not quoted.

rejected.option: Export the anchor and prefixes as pub consts from hestia.rs
rejected.why: hestia.rs is not a listed deliverable. A test built from the real generator gives the same protection.

decisions.choice: Finding 1: treat `work_decisions::approve_request` text as generated and cited. Anchor: the sentence 'A person approved this proposal from the steward role.' (work_decisions.rs:287). When the request holds the anchor, skip (a) lines starting 'Rung of the requirements ladder: ' (line 290), (b) the 'Proposal: ' line that holds ' (key ' and ' queued at ' (line 289), and (c) every line from the first line equal to '## Source' to the end (lines 291-306: the copied source file, cited job requests, commit texts and directory listings are cited content). The first line (the work item's title) and the sentences between stay plain prose and count.
decisions.reason: `approve_request` is the only Athena generator that writes a structural word as fixed text. Its output reaches the gate through `approve_work` (work_decisions.rs:330-331) and `ask`. The fake reader's default reading has capability change, one deliverable and no Term line, so without the skip every approval is refused: the athena-cli tests at work_decisions.rs:96-103 and drain.rs:5328, 6210, 6276 fail, and in production each approval is refused on its first read and replayed approvals count toward the 8% limit. Content copied from files and jobs is a citation, not the request's own use of a term. The same rule that exempts quoted and cited mentions covers it. The anchor and the exact line shapes keep a hand-written 'Rung of the requirements ladder: x' or '## Source' heading counted.

rejected.option: Edit approve_request to reword the rung line
rejected.why: work_decisions.rs is not a listed deliverable, and the line is the contract that tells the reader the rung of the work. Changing generated text to suit a check moves the fault.

rejected.option: Skip the whole request when it holds the anchor
rejected.why: The title is the steward's own wording of the work and is a real use; skipping everything would hide it.

rejected.option: Skip any '## Source' heading and 'Rung of the requirements ladder:' line with no anchor
rejected.why: A hand-written request with those lines would escape the check.

decisions.choice: Quote and parenthesis handling: remove straight and curly double-quoted spans, backtick pairs and single-quoted spans (opener after start/whitespace/`(` and before a letter or digit; closer after a non-space and before a non-alphanumeric; an unclosed opener stays as text). Scan per line. Remove a parenthesised span only if it has two or more commas or opens with e.g., i.e., such as, for example or like. Replace whitespace-delimited tokens containing `/`, `_` or `::` with a space.
decisions.reason: A single-comma parenthetical such as '(the ladder, which ranks requirements)' is a real use and stays counted; '(ladder, layer, tier)' has two commas and is dropped. Per-line scanning means a stray apostrophe cannot swallow the rest of the request.

rejected.option: Drop any parenthesised span that holds a comma
rejected.why: It hides a real use with a single comma.

decisions.choice: A term is defined by an assumption that, trimmed and lowercased, starts `term <word>:` followed by at least 3 words. A trailing `s` or `'s` on the word is dropped when the base is in STRUCTURAL_TERMS, so `Term layers:` defines layer. The line may cite the defining file.
decisions.reason: This copies the `Code survey:` convention (`code_surveys`, reading.rs:3832), which the reader already knows, and needs no new reading field.

decisions.choice: Finding 3: D164 lists every Athena request builder checked for fixed text with a structural word, and the 3% estimate is stated to cover hand-written requests only. Checked by grep for ladder, rung, tier, layer over crates/athena-core/src: `approve_request` (work_decisions.rs:290) is the only builder with fixed text holding a term, handled by the skip. `hestia::root_cause_request` carries the words only in earlier introspections' free text (skip by shape). `spec_request`, `throughput_request` and `slowdown_request` (hestia.rs:691, 1611, 1735) and the code_health builders (code_health.rs:550, 684) hold none. `steward::blind_spot_request` (steward.rs:754) holds none apart from its free `{title}`. `StewardRequest::from_change` (steward.rs:597) is the model's own words, counted like a hand-written request. `proposals::accept_request` (proposals.rs:442) holds none, and defaults.toml holds none. `audience::work_item` (audience.rs:98) reaches the gate through `approve_request`, and its title holds none. A corpus test runs the public `steward::blind_spot_change` request through the gate and expects acceptance.
decisions.reason: The replay share is measured over past requests, including generated ones. Naming what was checked and excluded makes the estimate honest and lets a later builder that adds a term be caught by review of D164.

rejected.option: Claim no generator is affected without listing them
rejected.why: That was the fault the finding names.

rejected.option: Count the generated approvals in the 3%
rejected.why: They are skipped by design, so they do not add to the share.

decisions.choice: Findings 2: the measurement path. The doc comment, CHANGELOG and D164 declare 'expected 3% of newly refused readings' as an estimate and say the measured share is recorded in the job's replay record at verification (`replay_stage`, then `run.record`). The producer sees a share only in a held send-back (`replay_problem`, run/producer.rs:61-68, 370-399), which is reported only when the share is over the limit (declared 3 + 5 = 8%). There is no at-or-under-8% branch. When a send-back arrives, the producer may change only `plain_request_prose` (the generated-line skips, the code-token skip, quote handling), never STRUCTURAL_TERMS, and reports the measured share in its output. D164 leaves the tier/layer decision to the user. No test asserts a measured figure.
decisions.reason: The loop sends work back only when the replay is held, so a measured figure at or under 8% never reaches the producer, and narrowing the word list conflicts with the brief.

rejected.option: Producer writes a measured figure when at or under 8%
rejected.why: That branch can never run.

rejected.why: The brief fixes the list; the choice is the user's.

rejected.option: A test needle for the measured share
rejected.why: The producer cannot know the share, so it cannot be satisfied reliably.
